descriptionChirho: To physically cut, carve, or inscribe marks into a hard surface such as stone, metal, or a tablet; the primary concrete sense of the root in Qal active forms, denoting the act of engraving or chiseling (Prov 8:27, 29; Isa 22:16; 30:8; 49:16; Ezek 4:1).

Passive of the engraving sense: to be carved, inscribed, or etched upon a surface, appearing in Hofal and Qal passive participle forms, expressing the resultant state of an inscription or carving (Job 19:23; Ezek 23:14).

To issue authoritative decrees, enact statutes, or establish binding ordinances; a metaphorical extension from inscribing into stone to the legislative act of fixing law, appearing in Piel and Pual stems (Prov 8:15; 31:5; Isa 10:1).

One who enacts laws or exercises governing authority, used as a substantivized Piel participle to designate a person of legislative or military command; applied to tribal leaders, rulers, and ultimately to God as Israel's lawgiver (Deut 33:21; Judg 5:9, 14; Isa 33:22).

The staff or scepter as the physical symbol of ruling authority, a metonymic development from 'one who decrees' to the instrument he holds; closely associated with tribal sovereignty and messianic promise (Gen 49:10; Num 21:18; Ps 60:7; 108:8).
